subject: Basic Technology
title: Fiji Year 10 Mock Examination 2 (2026 school format) — Basic Technology
instructions:
Answer ALL questions. Time allowed: 2 hours (an extra 10 minutes is allowed for reading).
Multiple-choice: click the letter of the best answer (click again to clear).
Short answers and paragraphs: type your answer in English in the box. Show working for calculations.
Your answers are saved automatically. The paper is submitted automatically when time runs out.
There are three sections. All are compulsory. All measurements are in millimetres unless stated otherwise.
Drawing questions use the drafting board (A4 landscape, 1 square = 5 mm). Tools: T-square, 45° and 30°/60° set squares, protractor, compass, pencil, ruler, eraser, text. Use THICK lines for outlines and THIN lines for construction. Press ⛶ to draw on a bigger screen.

sections.title: SECTION B  SHORT ANSWER QUESTIONS [50 marks]
sections.note: There are five questions in this section. All are compulsory. Use the drafting tools for the drawing parts (T-square, set squares, protractor, compass, pencil, eraser, text).

questions.text:
QUESTION 1 GENERAL KNOWLEDGE (10 marks)
PART A MATCHING (5 marks)
Match each term in List A with the correct description in List B. Two descriptions are not used.
options: A line of long and short dashes used for centre lines.
A board made of thin veneers glued with the grain at right angles.
A tool with a hardened point used to mark the centre before drilling.
Hand shears used to cut thin sheet metal.
A saw with a fine blade held in a frame, used to cut metal.
A joint where two pieces are cut at 45° to meet at a corner.
A thin line used to show hidden edges.

questions.text:
PART B (5 marks)
Figure 1 (right) is an isometric view of a stepped block. Its faces are lettered A to E.
Figure 2 (left) shows the block in third angle orthographic projection (front view, plan above it, left end view on its left). Its faces are numbered 1 to 5.
Write the letter of the face that matches each number, e.g. 1 = ?
questions.model:
1 = B (front of the upright, upper part of the front view) (1)
2 = A (top of the upright – back part of the plan) (1)
3 = D (front of the base, lower part of the front view) (1)
4 = E (left end – the L-shape in the end view) (1)
5 = C (top of the step – front part of the plan; in 3rd angle the front of the object is nearest the front view) (1)

questions.text:
QUESTION 2 TOOLS AND GEOMETRICAL CONSTRUCTIONS (10 marks)
PART A (2 marks)
A metal worker places a short steel tool with a hardened conical point on a marked cross and strikes it with a hammer to make a small dent before drilling.
(i) Give the complete name of the tool. (1 mark)
(ii) State the process being carried out. (1 mark)
PART C (1 mark)
Name the part of a jack plane that is turned to adjust the depth of cut (choose from: knob, lever cap, adjusting nut, frog).
questions.model:
PART A (i) Centre punch (1) (ii) Centre punching / marking the centre of a hole before drilling (so the drill does not slip) (1)
PART C Adjusting nut (1)

questions.text:
PART B (4 marks)
Given: A semi-ellipse is drawn above the major axis AB (120 mm). The minor axis CD is 70 mm.
Required:
(i) Find the two focal points of the ellipse by construction and label them F₁ and F₂. (2 marks)
(ii) Complete the ellipse by drawing the lower half below the major axis (concentric circles method or trammel method). (2 marks)
questions.model:
(i) Compass set to half the major axis (60 mm), centre C (end of minor axis), cut the major axis at F₁ and F₂ – about 48.7 mm either side of the centre O (1 each).
(ii) Lower half drawn as a smooth curve through constructed points, symmetrical to the upper half, passing through D (2; 1 if not smooth/inaccurate).

questions.text:
PART D (3 marks)
Given: A 30°/60° set square has its longest side (hypotenuse) 130 mm long. The 30° angle is at corner A.
Required: Draw the outline of the set square full size (scale 1:1), starting from corner A with the longest side horizontal. Label the 30°, 60° and 90° corners.
questions.model: Hypotenuse AB = 130 mm horizontal from A (1); 30° at A and 60° at B, so the right angle C is 112.6 mm from A and 65 mm from B (1); neat thick outline with angles labelled (1).

questions.text:
QUESTION 3 JOINTS AND HARDWARE (10 marks)
PART A (6 marks)
A wooden picture frame is made from four pieces of 40 mm × 20 mm timber. At each corner the two pieces meet at 45° so that no end grain shows on the face.
(i) Name a suitable joint for the corners of the frame. (1 mark – write it in the box)
(ii) Draw a neat pencil-rendered freehand pictorial sketch of ONE corner of the frame, with the two pieces pulled slightly apart to show the joint. Show the grain of the timber. (3 marks)
(iii) State the first two steps in preparing this joint. (2 marks – write them in the box)
questions.model:
(i) Mitre joint (1)
(ii) Pictorial sketch (isometric/oblique) of two members cut at 45°, shown slightly apart (1); correct proportion of 40 × 20 section (1); pencil rendering and grain lines along each piece (1).
(iii) Step 1: measure and mark the 45° line with a mitre square / sliding bevel (1). Step 2: cut accurately on the waste side with a tenon saw in a mitre box (1). (Then glue and nail/clamp.)

given.s: Sketch area – freehand pictorial sketch of one mitre corner.

questions.text:
PART B (2 marks)
(i) State two differences between a nail and a wood screw. (2 marks)
questions.model: Any two (1 each): a screw has a thread, a nail has a smooth shank; a screw is driven with a screwdriver, a nail with a hammer; a screw holds more strongly/does not pull out easily; a screw can be removed and reused without damage; a screw needs a pilot hole.

questions.text:
PART C (2 marks)
Draw a neat sketch of a BUTT HINGE (open flat) in the space provided. Show the two leaves, the knuckle and the countersunk screw holes.
questions.model: Two rectangular leaves joined at a central knuckle with a pin (1); countersunk screw holes on each leaf, correct proportions (1).

questions.text:
QUESTION 4 ISOMETRIC DRAWING (10 marks)
Given: A Shaped Block drawn in third angle orthographic projection (left side of the sheet) and the starting point A.
By taking measurements directly from the orthographic drawing (1 square = 5 mm), answer the following.
(i) Name the three views by writing FRONT ELEVATION, PLAN and END ELEVATION under the correct views with the Text tool. (2 marks)
(ii) Draw the Shaped Block in isometric drawing using the starting point A. Point A is the front bottom-left corner of the block. Use the 30° set square for the receding lines. (8 marks)
questions.model:
(i) Bottom-middle view = FRONT ELEVATION; view above it = PLAN; view on the left = END ELEVATION (left end view) (2; ½ off per error).
(ii) Correct starting point and isometric axes at 30° (1); base 70 × 40 × 20 (2); upright block from 25 mm to the right end with slope from 10 mm to 25 mm back rising 20 → 45 mm (2); top 15 mm wide at 45 mm high (1); correct line work – thick outlines, no hidden lines (1); accuracy and neatness (1).

given.s: Shaped Block - third angle projection (dimensions in mm)

questions.text:
QUESTION 5 SOLID GEOMETRY (10 marks)
Given: The elevation of a right cone (base Ø60 mm, height 70 mm) cut by an inclined plane, and the incomplete plan, in first angle orthographic projection. The apex V is shown with thin lines. Point O is given for the development.
Required:
(i) Complete the plan by showing the cut surface. (Divide the plan into 12 equal parts.) (3 marks)
(ii) Project the true shape of the section. (2 marks)
(iii) Develop the lateral surface of the truncated cone using the starting point O. (Exclude the base.) (4 marks)
(iv) Name the method of development used. (1 mark – write it in the box)
questions.model:
(i) 12 generators in plan and elevation (1); cut points projected down from the elevation to the plan (1); smooth closed curve (ellipse-like) drawn through them (1).
(ii) Projectors drawn at 90° to the cutting plane, widths transferred from the plan (1); smooth ellipse labelled TRUE SHAPE (1).
(iii) Sector radius = true length of generator √(30² + 70²) = 76.2 mm and angle = 360 × 30 ÷ 76.2 ≈ 142° (1); 12 equal divisions (1); true lengths of the cut points transferred from the outside generators of the elevation (1); smooth curve and seam lines (1).
(iv) Radial line development (1).

given.s: Truncated cone: base diameter 60, height 70 (to apex V).

sections.title: SECTION C  LONG ANSWER QUESTIONS [20 marks]
sections.note: There are two questions in this section. Both are compulsory.

questions.text:
SECTION C LONG ANSWER QUESTIONS (20 marks)
QUESTION 1 DESIGN (10 marks)
Problem: In many Fijian homes, shoes and slippers are left in a pile at the doorway. They get wet in the rain, people trip over them and pairs are easily lost.
Brief: Design a shoe rack for the doorway that will solve this storage problem.
Specifications:
• It must be made from a combination of timber and metal that are readily available.
• It must hold at least 6 pairs of shoes and let air flow so the shoes can dry.
• It must be strong, stable and portable.
• It must be easy to construct.
Requirements
(i) In the space provided, sketch a pictorial pencil/colour rendered final solution of the shoe rack. (4 marks)
questions.model: Correct proportion (½); correct line work (1); accuracy – meets the specifications: holds 6 pairs, open slats/rails for air flow, timber and metal (1); rendering shown (1); neatness (½).

questions.text: (ii) Draw a detailed sketch to show how the shelves are joined to the sides so that the rack stays strong and stable. In the box, state the finishing material used and one feature of the finish that suits Fiji's wet and humid climate. (4 marks)
questions.model:
Detailed sketch of the joint/fixing, e.g. housing joint or metal rods through drilled holes with nuts (correct proportion ½, line work ½, evidence of strength shown 1, neatness ½) (2½ → round with text).
Finishing material: varnish / exterior paint / wood oil / galvanised or painted metal (1).
Feature: water-resistant/protects timber from moisture, rot and borers; prevents rust (½–1).

questions.text:
(iii) Evaluate your final solution according to the following headings. (2 marks)
HEADING – FINAL SOLUTION
• Materials used: ...
• Ergonomics: ...
questions.model:
Materials used: names the timber (e.g. pine/mahogany) and metal (e.g. mild steel rod, galvanised screws) and says why they are suitable (1).
Ergonomics: suitable height so shoes can be placed without bending too much; no sharp edges; easy to lift/move (1).

questions.text:
QUESTION 2 ENTERPRISE AND COSTING (10 marks)
You decide to make and sell the shoe rack as a small school enterprise. The table shows the materials needed for ONE rack.
(i) Calculate the cost of materials for one rack. Show your working. (3 marks)
(ii) You add 40% to the cost of materials to cover labour and profit. Calculate the selling price of one rack. (2 marks)
(iii) How much profit will you make if you sell 8 racks and the labour cost is $6.00 per rack? (2 marks)
(iv) State two ways to advertise your shoe racks. (2 marks)
(v) State one safety precaution when applying varnish. (1 mark)
questions.model:
(i) Timber 4 × 6.50 = 26.00; rod 3 × 4.00 = 12.00; screws 5.50; varnish 0.5 × 18.00 = 9.00; sandpaper 2 × 1.25 = 2.50 (2) → Total $55.00 (1)
(ii) 55.00 × 1.40 (1) = $77.00 (1)
(iii) Profit per rack = 77.00 − 55.00 − 6.00 = $16.00 (1); 8 × 16.00 = $128.00 (1)
(iv) Any two (1 each): posters/notices at school; social media (Facebook page); word of mouth; display at school open day/market stall; flyers.
(v) Work in a well-ventilated area / wear gloves and a mask / keep away from flames (1).
